title: Few-shot code adaptation for a new KARC dynamical system
hypothesis: A compact system-specific Mirror coordinate over a frozen KARC feature bank will predict a newly encountered synthetic dynamical system with at least 25% fewer complete inference bytes than an independently stored readout, without worse heldout rollout error, and will improve on the native readout-adaptation control.

world.frozen_features: constant, state coordinates, quadratic cross terms, and fixed Fourier features
world.task_shift: system-specific coefficients; two systems include a nonlinear component outside the frozen bank

fresh.release_rule: Do not open fresh seeds after exact native readout alias or a strict gate miss.

controls: shared frozen feature bank with no system code
Mirror-coded readout over the same frozen bank
basis-growth control that stores private residual features where required
success_gate: PASS only if the Mirror payload preserves rollout nRMSE <=0.02, uses at least 25% fewer bytes than independent readouts, and is strictly better in bytes/quality than native closed-form readout adaptation.
failure_gate: FAIL if native readout adaptation exactly aliases Mirror, the shared basis misses quality, or the byte/quality gate is missed.
boundaries: Synthetic four-dimensional systems only; not trained KARC or real continual-learning evidence.
System-specific support-derived readouts are stored at inference, so this does not test zero-shot unseen-system generalization.
Basis-growth residuals are counted as persistent bytes.
No fresh evaluation after native alias or gate miss.
